notes: §1985:XI.4.1.4 GR6: 'The results of the merge operation are undefined unless the records in the files referenced by file-name-2 and file-name-3 are ordered as described in the ASCENDING or DESCENDING KEY phrases'; so the compiler owes a correct merge of ordered input and nothing for unordered input. EmitMerge starts one stream per USING file (SortNextInput) and CobolSort.Merge has SortWork.SequenceMerge k-way-merge the streams by the keys; SortWork.CheckOrder's EC-SORT-MERGE-SEQUENCE test is the 2023 addition, and any result for unordered input is within 1985's 'undefined'. Probes at 85: witness (AAA CCC / BBB DDD) gives AAA BBB CCC DDD; class d/f: three USING files merged on DESCENDING alphanumeric major and ASCENDING SIGN LEADING SEPARATE minor keys give B+0011 B+0092 A-0993 A-0021 A+0051 A+0052 (ties in USING-file order); S9(18) COMP-3 keys from -999999999999999999 through 999999999999999999 merge in numeric order; unordered input (A then B under a DESCENDING key) runs to the end with exit 0 and an interleaved result, which 1985 leaves undefined. Classes a, b, c, e: GR6 has no syntax arm, edition phrase or organization case of its own.

next.reason: 1985: "The results of the merge operation are undefined unless the records ... are ordered as described in the ASCENDING or DESCENDING KEY phrases"; 2023: "the EC-SORT-MERGE-SEQUENCE exception condition is set to exist, all files associated with the MERGE statement are closed, and the results ... undefined". Out-of-order input still gives undefined merge results, but 2023 adds defined effects: the EC-SORT-MERGE-SEQUENCE exception is set and all files of the MERGE are closed.
